rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters deny a reality that is as evident as the midday sun.
rows.anchor: they are denying a reality which is shinning over their heads like the midday sun.

rows.speaker: lexicographers
rows.claim: Lexicographers explain the phrase as a mixed or tangled affair, meaning a situation of clear contradiction and conflict.
rows.anchor: by lexicographers as أﻣﺮ ﻣﺨﺘﻠﻂand أﻣﺮ ﻣﻠﺘﺒﺲ which means a situation in which there is a very clear contradiction and conflict.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root maraja means to mix; the Qur'anic usage in 55:19 illustrates the word's sense of things meeting after being let loose.
rows.anchor: means to mix up. In S ūrah al-Raḥmān, it is said:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters affirm God and attributes that entail Judgement while denying that very consequence, leaving them in mental conflict that the Qur'an alone resolves.
rows.anchor: they were in a state of contradiction with regard to their views, for on the one hand, they affirm God and all His attributes which necessitate the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who deny truth fashion excuses to justify themselves, but each excuse only exposes the baselessness of their position.
rows.anchor: whatever excuse a person tries to fashion out only brings out the baselessness of his stance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi connects this contradiction to the counterpart sūrah al-Dhāriyāt, which calls the rejecters deeply contradictory.
rows.anchor: The Qur’ ān has pointed to this contradiction of stance in Sūrah al-Dhāriyāt the counterpart of this sūrah in the following words:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi directs readers to al-Naml for a fuller treatment of the rejecters' doubt about the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: This issue has been fully explained in S ūrah Naml under the following verse:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance grows when laziness gathers correct and incorrect views together or when desire blends falsehood with truth, making life contradictory.
rows.anchor: either because of laziness he gathers in his mind all kinds of correct and incorrect views or while pursuing his whims and desires

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person can resist Satan's trials by examining beliefs, keeping critical judgment alive, and refusing to mix evil with truth; few do so.
rows.anchor: If a person keeps analyzing his views, does not allow his critical ability to die away and in pursuance of whims and desires

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky and earth display God's power, wisdom, and providence; these evident signs can awaken anyone whose heart is receptive to truth.
rows.anchor: First and foremost, attention is directed to His great power and wisdom:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised, star-adorned, uncracked heaven displays such power and wisdom that recreation cannot be difficult for its Creator.
rows.anchor: The implication is that how can recreation be difficult for someone whose majesty of power and wisdom they see above their heads?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spread earth, stabilizing mountains, and varied vegetation provide and delight people; the Provider will also call them to account.
rows.anchor: Will the Lord Who has made such arrangements for their nourishment leave them to eat, live and be merry without calling them to account.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs serve insight and reminder, jolting attentive hearts from indifference, but affect only those open to them.
rows.anchor: enough to open eyes and jolt and awaken hearts; however, these miracles can only be effective for those who are ready to accept their influence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's terms convey insight beyond outward appearances and a reminder that rouses people from apathy.
rows.anchor: means to create insight so that they are able to go past the external form and see what is beneath it, while the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's diversity and beauty are not needed for bare existence; God displays them to awaken perception of power, wisdom, beauty, and generosity.
rows.anchor: this world did not require for its existence and sustenance the diversity, variety and tint which is evident from every nook and corner of it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Materialists who lose their subtle perception find the universe dark and fail to learn the wisdom written throughout it.
rows.anchor: for people who by becoming slaves to the material world have lost this subtle sense in them, this universe is a place of pitch darkness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people an innate capacity for reminder and free will; using their understanding brings more light, while ingratitude forfeits what they were given.
rows.anchor: If he does so, he is blessed with more light from God, otherwise whatever had been given to him is confiscated

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi links the resurrection argument to 17:99: the Creator of heaven and earth has power to create people again.
rows.anchor: Do they not see that the God Who has created the heavens and the earth has power to create their like?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fuller account in 79:27–33 invokes creation of the sky, earth, water, fodder, and mountains to establish God's power, greatness, wisdom, and providence.
rows.anchor: A deliberation on these verses will show that they contain all the aspects of power, greatness, wisdom and providence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly and earthly signs display harmony and thereby argue for God's oneness.
rows.anchor: there is found great harmony between the two.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The providential benefits of the signs entail that people will face reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: The elements of providence found in them necessitate reward and punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain reviving barren land makes life after death imaginable, just as dead ground becomes alive after rain.
rows.anchor: the way rain enlivens a barren piece of land also brings the scenario of life after death before a person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain expression means rain that brings lushness and luxuriance.
rows.anchor: refers to rain which is a means of lushness and luxuriance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the rain blessed distinguishes the life-giving rain here from rain that brings destruction or punishment.
rows.anchor: At times, rain causes havoc and destruction instead of luxuriance and it assumes the form of punishment for nations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orchards provide fresh, delicious fruit, while harvested crops provide nutrition that can be stored and used continuously.
rows.anchor: created for them fresh and delicious fruit in orchards and nutritional crops which can be stored once they are harvested and can be benefited from continuously.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Date palms are named after the general category of gardens because dates were an especially valuable local fruit and nutritional resource for Arabia.
rows.anchor: the reason that a specific category has been mentioned after the general one is that this was a special grain found in Arabia

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The height of the date palms and their clustered fruit should awaken observation and gratitude.
rows.anchor: Reference to the height of the date palms and to the clusters of dates is to awaken the sense of observation and the feeling of gratitude

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orderly clusters reveal the Creator's lavish power, wisdom, and creativity, while the benefits impose an obligation for which people will be questioned.
rows.anchor: The layered clusters of dates bear witness from their very form that the Creator has so copiously used His power, wisdom and creativity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be questioned about the divine favours they received.
rows.anchor: they shall one day be questioned about them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival of dead land by rain is the sūrah's central theme and analogizes the resurrection that its rejecters deem impossible.
rows.anchor: Rising of the dead should be regarded analogous to this with which they are being informed of; however, they regard it to be impossible.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi warns Quraysh that Noah's people, al-Rass, Thamūd, ʿĀd, Pharaoh, Lot's brethren, al-Aykah, and Tubbaʿ denied after proof and were punished; Quraysh's persistent rejection will also bring punishment.
rows.anchor: the people of Noah (sws) the dwellers of the al-Rass valley, the Tham ūd, the ‘ Ād, the Pharaoh, the brethren of Lot

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice brings punishment once the truth has been conclusively conveyed and rejected.
rows.anchor: This is a reference to the practice of God which necessarily comes into play once the truth is conclusively conveyed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse returns to the warning first mentioned in verse 5 after presenting arguments for the Hereafter, now illustrating the fate of earlier rejecters.
rows.anchor: after referring towards it, the direction of the discourse changed to arguments which substantiate the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi points to his discussion of the companions of al-Rass in al-Furqān 25:38, where he reviewed exegetes' opinions and stated his preference.
rows.anchor: The companions of al-Rass have been mentioned in verse 38

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the nations are not listed chronologically, al-Rass follows Noah because its people were among ancient Arab peoples whose history was mostly lost.
rows.anchor: Though nations are not cited here in chronological sequence, yet the mention of the companions of al-Rass right after the people of Noah (sws) shows that they belonged to the ancient nations of Arabia

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates that the companions of al-Rass denied their messenger and were consequently destroyed by God's punishment.
rows.anchor: show that the companions of al-Rass denied the messenger sent to it. As a result, the punishment of God visited them and destroyed them.

rows.speaker: exegetical works
rows.claim: Exegetical narratives say the people of al-Rass buried their messenger in a well.
rows.anchor: A narrative recorded in exegetical works says that these people had buried their messenger in a well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rass means a well, which is why these people are called the companions of al-Rass.
rows.anchor: The word rass means a well and thus these people came to be known as the companions of al-Rass.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi doubts the story: there is no authentic evidence that a nation killed its messenger, and the name's meaning does not prove this particular incident.
rows.anchor: However, this report does not seem to be true. There is no authentic information regarding a messenger being killed by his nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pharaoh is singled out because he was the actual culprit who misled his people, as also stated in 20:79 and 79:17.
rows.anchor: for Pharaoh misled his people: he did not guide them, (20:79)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi refers readers to his discussion of Tubbaʿ in the exegesis of Sūrah al-Dukhān.
rows.anchor: The nation of Tubba‘ are mentioned in the exegesis of Sūrah al-Dukhān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God created the heavens and earth initially, people should not doubt his ability to create them again after death.
rows.anchor: do not such people see the heavens and the earth created by God; was He unable to create them the first time.
